A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CSPO study with 18 pages, including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment: pages 2–18 are identical, and the first-page changes are fully readable.

before.justification: v1 reports original table-to-LaTeX benchmark experiments, ablations, human–LLM agreement measurements and evaluator-stability results in Section 6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark comparisons, ablations and evaluator-validation outcomes in Section 6 and Appendix F, including the numerical results in Tables 1–4 and 6–11.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same component decomposition, binary component rewards, token-specific credit assignment, global TEDS/compilation rewards and policy objectives. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions train on TableTex and evaluate on TableTex-test, DocGenome-table-1k and Table2LaTeX-test-simple (Section 6.1, Tables 1–2). Dataset, domain and task coverage are identical.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5 Flash, Nougat, Qwen2.5-VL baselines, GRPO and VSGRPO in Tables 1–2, and SFT comparisons in Tables 3–4 and 9.

E3.justification: Both retain the 15,000/4,000 TableTex training/test split, 3B/7B models, SFT/RL training budgets and greedy decoding. Evaluation metrics, judge configurations and human-evaluation procedures are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.3 and Appendix F retain identical reward-aggregation, global-reward, component, weight and reward-granularity ablations. Evaluator-reliability analyses, training curves and qualitative success/failure cases are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both already report eight GPT-4o evaluations of the same 4,000 predictions, with means and variances in Appendix F.2 and Table 11. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are identical, including appendix results. For example, Table 1 retains Overall Fidelity of 45.2% and 53.0% for 3B and 7B CSPO, respectively, versus 42.0% and 50.6% for corresponding GRPO baselines.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives in Sections 3–5, the TEDS definition in Appendix A and the objective derivation in Appendix D are identical. No formal reasoning is added, removed or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about reward ambiguity, CSPO and hierarchical evaluation. The added code-availability sentence does not alter these contributions or performance claims.

C2.justification: Result interpretations are identical. Section 9 retains the limitations concerning fidelity, training-data scale and LLM-evaluation cost; Appendix G retains the same generalization and training-cost discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and the microsoft/CSPO GitHub repository address to the abstract; v1 provides no such pointer. Existing implementation settings, evaluation prompts and training-cost disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are identical, including positioning relative to DocGenome, LATTE, GRPO and Ling et al.'s table-to-LaTeX reinforcement-learning work.

P1.justification: v2 expands the institutional affiliations, adds Peng Cheng Laboratory for Jitao Sang, inserts the abstract's code-availability sentence and updates the arXiv version/date text. Remaining prose and section organization are identical.

P2.justification: Minor first-page spacing and reflow accommodate the expanded affiliations and abstract. No figures or tables are added, removed or redrawn; pages 2–18 render identically.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer modestly improves implementation discoverability and reproducibility documentation. Scientific arguments, empirical evidence and appendices remain unchanged. This is a limited documentation benefit; the PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or usability.
